page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-2 is a compute-focused instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs spanning a single physical core with multithreading enabled, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. System memory totals 4.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The server configuration includes no local storage volumes and no GPU hardware accelerators, relying entirely on external volumes for disk storage.

Benchmark evaluations highlight a contrast between single-core throughput and aggregate scaling. The instance achieves strong results in stress-ng single-core execution alongside average single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core scores. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics such as Geekbench multi-core, software compilation, and ray tracing fall into lower performance percentiles due to the two-thread execution ceiling. Memory benchmarks also exhibit constrained throughput, with uncached read speeds measuring 31.59 GB/sec and uncached write speeds at 23.42 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-highcpu-2 delivers dedicated AMD core performance without requiring allocation for large memory pools or bundled local NVMe drives. The absence of integrated storage and hardware accelerators makes it unsuited for heavy database manipulation or high-concurrency systems. Instead, the profile aligns with lightweight web serving, continuous integration build runners, small microservices, and single-threaded batch tasks requiring predictable execution without high memory overhead.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-2 is an entry-tier compute-optimized virtual machine equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the configuration pairs 4.0 GB of system memory at a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 32 MB of L3 cache, but includes neither local storage nor onboard GPU accelerators. Performance metrics demonstrate capable single-threaded execution, evidenced by strong stress-ng single-core figures and average single-threaded compression throughput. However, overall multi-core computational capacity and memory bandwidth remain constrained due to the two-thread limit and minimal RAM footprint. Cost efficiency is driven by dedicated CPU access at a compact scale, avoiding overprovisioning costs for lightweight services. The c2d-highcpu-2 is best suited for light microservices, continuous integration runners, lightweight background tasks, and basic web serving that prioritize single-thread throughput over aggregate parallel scaling or high memory capacity.
